title: EnFractal room state (saved play on top of a room manifest)
description: Everything play has changed in a room: moved or removed objects, creations, locks, avatar identities, the active style, the durable receipt ledger and, since Run 2, the team's journal and discovered map. The scene is rebuilt from manifest + state; no other scene state is authoritative. Written atomically per docs/engine/persistence-notes.md. Velocities, running effects, goals, jobs, what an avatar is holding (a carried thing is saved where it was last put down) and transient receipts are not saved. When a checkpoint is taken, receipts at or below its revision may be compacted; receipt.lookup then reports compacted.

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the room.json bytes this state was built on. A mismatch means the room was re-exported and the state needs an explicit migration.

rules.description: Kernel versions that interpreted this state.

store_revision.description: Equals the room revision of the last committed command.

session.description: Writer fence: a stale session must not overwrite a newer revision.

entities.description: Keyed by entity id. Captured objects appear here only once play has changed them.

receipts.description: Keyed by principal|action_id. Bounded; see persistence notes for the reserved recovery path.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the canonical command JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace).

result.description: Only successful, durable command results are kept here.

journal.description: The team's journal (docs/companion/JOURNAL.md), saved with the room. A room state written before Run 2 has none: read its absence as an empty journal.

history.description: Facts and finished tasks, oldest first. At most 500 (start): the oldest 'found' and 'gathered' entries of finished tasks go first; 'built' and 'changed' are kept.

notes.description: The companion's notes, oldest first. At most 100 (start), the oldest dropped first; the player may remove any.

discovered.description: What the team has discovered of this room, saved with it: only the two avatars' eyes add to it, never the camera and never anything the AI says. A room state written before Run 2 has none: read its absence as nothing discovered yet, so the map starts blank.

cell_m.description: Edge of one cell of discovered space, in metres (start: 0.05).

entities.description: Every discovered object and creation as the team last saw it, keyed by id. At most 1,024 (start): out-of-sight routine entries go first, least recently seen; things the team built and the resources of an open task are kept. The shell and the avatars are always known and are not listed.

extensions.description: Experiments (common.schema.json). The kernel host writes its own blocks here under x_play_: among them x_play_nature, the island's nature (the ground's cells, what fire did to each object and creation, the trail, the weather clock and the latest nature changes' undo steps), checked whole before anything is restored. Other readers ignore them. Since P-Inventory-2 x_play_nature writes no wallet (decision 116: logs and stones are stacks); an older one is read and its counts become the chest's stacks on load; it keeps loose, the units set down on the island (decision 118: each a kind and its bottom centre in the room, at most 256, the oldest going first). Since the mechanics round two keys are typed here: x_clock, the island's clock, and x_team, whose save this is and how it plays (written by the teams packet, M3, and the clock's, M6); and since P-Inventory x_play_camp's chest, the island's one chest.

revision.description: Entity revision, incremented on each change to this entity.

removed.description: Gone from the room, kept at the pose it had. An object the island's nature burned down is removed at the pose it burned at (the manifest is never edited); a host that restores it reads why from its nature extension (the kernel host's x_play_nature) and refuses a removal nothing accounts for.

source.description: The editable garage_game.creation source; the compiled artifact is derived again on load, never trusted from the file.

transformed_from.description: Entity this creation replaced through entity.transform; identity and protection carry over.

support_ids.description: Entities this one rests on; they are protected from changes that would undermine it.

discovered_level.description: Discovered space on one level, a walkable surface patch at one height (the floor, the top of the big box, a shelf). A grid in room coordinates from min_xz_m, +x along a row and +z from row to row. Cell (column c, row r) is bit r * columns + c of the cells bitmap, least significant bit first in each byte; 1 means discovered.

support.description: The shell part, object or creation whose walkable top this level is.

surface.description: Which of the support's walkable surfaces (its asset's walkable_surfaces id), when it has several.

cells.description: Standard base64 (with padding) of exactly ceil(columns * rows / 8) bytes; the unused bits of the last byte are 0.

discovered_entity.description: One discovered entity as the team last saw it.

entity.description: Its summary as last seen. Holding is not saved, and the knowledge fields are worked out when the host answers.

may_be_stale.description: The sticky bit: it changed in some way since the team last saw it (moved, changed, locked, picked up or gone), never saying which. The host adds the age rule when it answers.

x_clock.description: The island's clock (docs/game/MECHANICS.md section 9): in the room state's open extension, which a save may change, never in the pinned manifest, whose every change starts a fresh save. The sun and the sky read the time through one WorldTime(utcNow, clock) (M6; the kernel keeps the record as CommandHost.ClockRecord and the boot hands it to the look). The weather reads no clock: it runs on a counter saved with the island's nature (x_play_nature), so in Live, where every team shares one island, it follows that shared state and every team sees the same rain (the founder, 15 October). Absent, or day_scale 1 with no phase: the machine's own clock, today's behaviour. Live will use four game days a real day. The island save does not carry this record yet; an imported room state does.

zone_id.description: The world owner's time zone, an IANA id (Etc/UTC, Europe/Paris): the time of day, daylight saving and the calendar follow it, and the day rolls over at dawn. A zone, never a place.

day_scale.description: Game days per real day, a divisor of 24 so that nothing drifts: 1 is the real clock (the default, no change until Live); Live's 4 makes a day 6 real hours, with midnight at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 world-local.

seasons_per_year.description: Seasons follow the real calendar, four a year of about 91 real days each: 4 only, for now (the founder, 15 October).

phase_h.description: An offset in game hours, so an evening-only child still meets night (0: none).

hemisphere.description: Which half of the year is summer.

x_team.description: Whose island save this is and how it plays (the mechanics round; written by the teams packet, M3): the team (contracts/team.schema.json), the mode and, in Challenge, its difficulty, chosen at the opening menu and fixed for the save, which never changes its mode (decided: switching modes means switching saves). Absent: today's single player, in the mode the player's profile holds.

x_play_camp.description: The kernel host's camp block (Fire's camp: the start spots, the lit campfires, the camp the player wakes at; its other keys are the kernel's own and open here), which since P-Inventory also carries the island's one chest (chest), shared by every campsite (decision 102). The island save keeps the same block in its team block's camp.

chest.description: The island's chest (P-Inventory): stacks by kind, and the ids of the unique things in it, each a room object of this island kept as a removed entity (marked gathered in the kernel's nature block) until it is taken out with its own id. Absent: an empty chest; an empty chest writes no key. The chest never spills (decision 101), and the Creative copy into Challenge starts empty.
